title: PNT Error Term: Can We Sharpen to O(√x log x)?

problemStatement.informal: Can the Prime Number Theorem error term be sharpened to O(√x log x)? Von Koch (1901) showed this is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis.
problemStatement.formal: RiemannHypothesis ↔ ∃ C > 0, ∀ x ≥ 2, |(primePi x : ℝ) - logIntegral x| ≤ C * sqrt x * log x

knownResults: Von Koch (1901): RH ⟺ |π(x) − Li(x)| = O(√x log x)
Unconditional best: O(x · exp(−c(log x)^{3/5}(log log x)^{−1/5})) — Korobov–Vinogradov (1958)
Under RH: prime gaps pₙ₊₁ − pₙ = O(√pₙ log pₙ)
Cramér's conjecture: pₙ₊₁ − pₙ = O(log²pₙ) — open, not known from RH
